description: Shared fixture for the Go and Python future-format skip tests (go/version_test.go, py/test_validate.py). Both tests append these two entries to the committed suite, raise format_version, and require the entries to be SKIPPED rather than rejected -- which is what the MUST-skip rule promises: a new vector shape can be added without breaking an existing validator. Each entry deliberately carries members no current build has a field or a member set for (`tier`, `attestation`, `provenance`, `witness`) and an `expect` token no current build knows, so a validator that strict-decodes before deciding to skip fails the whole file. The same tests re-run both entries at min_format_version 2, where they must be rejected AS unknown members: without that control the skip assertion would pass even if these members were not actually unknown.

input.attestation: a v3 member on a checkpoint

tips.provenance: a v3 member on a tip

negative.name: future_format_negative
negative.reason: a v3 rejection reason no current build has a name for

input.attestation: a v3 member on a checkpoint

tips.provenance: a v3 member on a tip

chain.witness: a v3 member on a signed chain prefix wrapper
